description: Two workers must not independently change a shared surface, even when they are editing different files. File disjointness is necessary and not sufficient.
rationale: A backend agent editing the API implementation and a frontend agent editing the client both change the API contract. Their files never collide; the contract does. The result is a merge that compiles and a system that does not work.

coupled_surfaces.rule: The contract is agreed and recorded before either side implements. Implementers consume it; they do not amend it.
One owner per migration sequence. Two parallel migrations against one table are sequenced, never parallelised.
One owner per environment surface. Application changes request configuration; they do not write it.
Producer and consumer changes are sequenced around a compatible intermediate state, never landed together.
One writer per key. A flag read by two services is owned by one of them.

the_pattern: 1. The surface owner produces or amends the contract, and it is reviewed.
3. Only then do implementers work in parallel, each consuming the contract.
4. An implementer that finds the contract wrong raises it with the owner. It does not amend it.

enforcement.declared: Each workflow stage lists the coupled_artifacts it may touch.
enforcement.checked: scripts/validate_plugin.py fails when two stages that may run in parallel declare the same coupled surface.
enforcement.not_enforceable_mechanically: Nothing stops two agents reasoning about the same contract in prose. The control is that the contract artifact has one owner and a review gate, not that the files are disjoint.
